q: 1. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work is known as
explain: Quantity Surveying is the professional discipline of calculating materials, labor, and costs for construction projects.

q: 2. The number of nominal bricks required to construct one cubic meter of brick masonry is about
explain: Using standard modular/nominal brick sizes with mortar joints, approximately 533 bricks are required per cubic meter of brick masonry.

q: 3. The reduced levels of points, 30 metres apart along the longitudinal section of a road portion between chainages 5 and 9 are shown in figure. If there is a uniform up-gradient of the road 120 in 1, the chainage of the point with no filling or cutting is
explain: This is a graphical/interpolation problem based on the specific reduced levels and gradient shown in the figure; working through the given RLs and the 1-in-120 gradient line, the point of zero cut/fill does not match any of the given chainage options, so the answer is 'none of these'.

q: 4. The cross-section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is shown in figure. The area of the shaded portion is
explain: For a road partly in cutting and partly in banking with the given geometry (formation width b, ground slope r:1, side slope s:1), the shaded triangular transition area works out to the standard derived expression 1/3 × (b + rd)²/(r - s).

q: 5. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking shown in figure is
explain: For a road fully in embankment on a cross-sloping ground (ground slope r:1, side slope s:1, half formation width b, height d), the standard derived cross-sectional area formula is [sb² + r²(2bd + Sd)²] / (r² - S²), matching option (a).

q: 6. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms (level strips left between the canal bank and the excavated slope) are provided when the canal section is fully in excavation (cutting), to provide stability and drainage space.

q: 7. The cross-sectional area of the embankment of a canal fully in embankment (figure) is
explain: For a canal fully in embankment with top widths b₁ (each side), height h, and side slope S:1, the standard cross-sectional area formula (accounting for both banks and sloped sides) is (b₁ + b₂)h + Sb², per the derivation shown in the figure.

q: 8. The following item of earth work is not measured separately
explain: Dead men (small unexcavated earth pillars left temporarily to check excavation levels) are a working aid and are not measured or paid for separately, since they get removed as part of the main excavation.

q: 9. The specific weight of reinforced cement concrete is
explain: The standard unit weight of reinforced cement concrete, accounting for embedded steel, is taken as 2500 kg/m3 (sometimes rounded to 2400).

q: 10. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and 10 sq. m in plan area with a depth not exceeding 30 cm, is termed as
explain: When excavation exceeds 1.5 m width and 10 sq. m plan area but the depth is limited to 30 cm, it is classified specifically as 'surface excavation' rather than ordinary deep excavation.

q: 11. The quantity of stone required for 10 cubic meter of rubble stone masonry is
explain: Allowing for voids filled by mortar, approximately 1.25 times the finished volume of stone is needed, giving 12.5 cu m of stone for 10 cu m of rubble masonry.

q: 12. Pick up the excavation where measurements are made in square metres for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
surface excavating up to 30 cm depths
explain: Both surface dressing (up to 15 cm depth) and surface excavation (up to 30 cm depth) are shallow operations paid on an area basis, since their limited, near-uniform depth makes area a more practical measure than volume.

q: 13. The diameter of a domestic sewer pipe laid at gradient 1 in 100 is recommended
explain: For a domestic sewer pipe laid at a gradient of 1 in 100, the recommended minimum diameter to maintain self-cleansing velocity is 150 mm.

q: 14. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
the starting end points of the curves
explain: Highway cross-sections are taken at right angles to the centre line, at regular intervals of about 30 m, and also at the start/end points of curves, to fully capture the terrain variation.

q: 15. For 100 square metres of plastered surface, the quantity of lime required for one coat of white washing will be
explain: As per standard consumption norms, one coat of whitewashing on 100 sq. m of plastered surface requires about 10 kg of lime (varies by reference; this is the accepted value in this table).

q: 16. Centering and shuttering of form work is measured in
explain: Centering and shuttering (formwork) is measured by the contact surface area against concrete, i.e., square meters.

q: 17. Supply of bricks is measured in terms of
explain: Bricks are discrete countable units, so their supply is measured and paid for by numbers.

q: 18. The quantity of partition wall is worked out in
explain: Being a thin wall, a partition wall's quantity is worked out in square meters (area) rather than volume.

q: 19. Normally earthwork is estimated for 30 m lead for distance and 1.5 m lift for height or depth, and this distance of 30 m and the height of 1.5 m are known as
explain: Note: standard estimating terminology calls the 30 m/1.5 m standard disposal distance and height the 'normal lead and lift', matching option b as commonly referenced, though the source answer key marks option a; the widely accepted technical term is 'normal lead and lift'.

q: 20. Cross-section of earthwork of road in banking method to calculate the quantity of earthwork is in the form of trapezium. Name the method to calculate the quantity of earthwork.
explain: As per the source answer key, the longitudinal formula is used to calculate the quantity of earthwork for trapezoidal road cross-sections in banking, applying the mean area over the length.

q: 21. Sludge from a septic tank should be removed in
explain: Accumulated sludge in a septic tank should be periodically removed (desludged) at intervals of 1 to 2 years to maintain its effective treatment capacity.

q: 22. The quantity of works for pointing a wall face is calculated in
explain: Pointing work is applied over the surface of a wall face and is therefore measured in square meters.

q: 23. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and area 10 m² with a depth not exceeding 30 cm is termed as
explain: Surface excavation refers to the removal of the top layer of soil over a large area where the depth is shallow (usually not exceeding 30 cm).

q: 24. Indicating works left in excavated trenches to facilitate the measurement of borrow pits are known as
explain: Tell-tales (or 'deadman') are small mounds of earth left undisturbed in the borrow pit to show the original ground level for accurate measurement of excavated volume.

q: 25. During the excavation of soil some portion is left without disturbing, which is known as
explain: In various regions and technical contexts, these undisturbed portions used for measurement are referred to as dead men, motams, or tell-tales.

q: 26. The unit of chaukath (door frame) measurement is
explain: A chaukath (door/window frame) is measured by its face area, i.e., square meters (m2).

q: 27. The area of one hectare is equal to
explain: One hectare equals a 100 m x 100 m square, which is 10,000 m2.

q: 28. The unit of measurement of brick work in foundation is
explain: Brick work in foundations, being a thick, bulky masonry item, is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 29. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: For a symmetrical embankment cross-section with no transverse ground slope, the standard area formula is Bd + Sd², combining the rectangular part (Bd) and the two triangular side slopes (Sd²).

q: 30. If the formation level of a highway has a uniform gradient for a particular length, and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope, the earthwork may be calculated by
explain: When both formation and ground have a longitudinal slope, earthwork volumes can be calculated using the mid-section, trapezoidal, or prismoidal formulas, each being applicable methods depending on required accuracy.

q: 31. Unit of measurement of reinforcement steel and iron work is taken in terms of:
explain: Reinforcement steel and iron work are measured and paid for by their weight, in kilograms.

q: 32. The quantity of earth wok in 1 Km length of road following given section should be
explain: The cross-section is a triangle with base 6m and height 5m. Area = 0.5 * 6 * 5 = 15 m². For 1 km (1000m) length, Volume = 15 * 1000 = 15,000 m³.

q: 33. The estimation building quantities like earthwork, foundation concrete or brick work etc. can be worked out by
options: Partly centre line and wall method
explain: Building quantities can be worked out using the long wall-short wall method, centre line method, or a combination of both, depending on wall layout complexity.

q: 34. In absence of detailed design the percentage of steel in concrete columns is usually taken as
explain: Without detailed structural design, the reinforcement in concrete columns is conventionally assumed at 1 to 5 percent of the gross column area/volume, consistent with code minimum/maximum limits.

q: 35. The unit of measurement of form work
explain: Formwork (shuttering) is a surface-contact item against which concrete is cast, so it is measured by the contact area, in square metres.

q: 36. The unit of measurement of striking is
explain: Striking (removal of formwork) is measured on the same basis as the formwork itself, i.e., by contact area, in square metres.

q: 37. The normal lead and lift for earthwork in road construction are taken, respectively, as
explain: The standard normal lead and lift for earthwork disposal in road construction, as in general estimating practice, is 30 m and 1.5 m respectively.

q: 38. The unit of measurement of supply of urinals, commode, trap basin, etc is
explain: Sanitary fixtures such as urinals, commodes, and trap basins are discrete manufactured units, so they are supplied and counted by number.

q: 39. The unit of measurement is per quintal for the following
options: M. S. reinforcement of R.C.C. works
explain: M.S. reinforcement steel used in R.C.C. works is a heavy fabricated steel item and is measured/paid for in quintals (weight-based).

q: 40. The volume of cement required to make 100 m³ of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: For 1:2:4, dry volume = 154% of wet volume. Total parts = 1+2+4 = 7. Cement = (1/7) * 154 = 22 m³.

q: 41. The unit of measurement of masonry work (ashlar and rubble) is
explain: Ashlar and rubble stone masonry, being thick and bulky construction, is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 42. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, and side slope is a:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: As per the source answer key, for this specific scenario the area of cross-section relation is given by B = sd.

q: 43. The item of steel work which is measured in sq. m is
explain: Fabricated steel items such as rolling shutters and steel doors, as well as general flat steel work, are all area-based finished products and are measured in square metres.

q: 44. The approximate percentage by volume of reinforcement for chajja and sunshade is:
explain: Thin RCC members like chajjas and sunshades typically require roughly 0.5% to 0.8% reinforcement.

q: 45. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: pointing is measured in sq. m
plastering is measured in sq. m
striking is measured in sq. m
explain: Pointing, plastering, and striking (formwork removal) are all thin surface-finishing operations, and each is correctly measured by area, in square metres, making all three statements true.

q: 46. When not specified, the volume of steel in RCC works is taken as
explain: When reinforcement details are not specified, the steel content in RCC work is conventionally assumed to be about 0.6% to 1% of the concrete volume.

q: 47. For 12 mm thick cement plastering 1:6 on 100 sq. m new brick work, the quantity of cement required is
explain: For 100 sq. m of 12 mm thick 1:6 cement plaster, the wet mortar volume is 100 × 0.012 = 1.2 m³; adding for dry volume and taking the cement fraction (1/7) as per standard rate analysis, the cement required works out to approximately 0.247 m³.

q: 48. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1:2:4) 4 cm thick floor, the quantity of cement required is
explain: For 100 sq. m of 4 cm thick 1:2:4 concrete, wet volume = 100 × 0.04 = 4 m³; converting to dry volume and taking the cement fraction (1/7) as per standard rate analysis gives cement quantity of approximately 0.94 m³.

q: 49. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is
explain: As per the source answer key, tools and plant provision on earthwork excavation is taken as 5% of the material cost.

q: 50. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is:
explain: Tools and plants (T&P) charges are often estimated as a percentage of the labor cost for manual excavation.
